name: llmc_layernorm_backward
goal: Port layernorm_backward_harness.cu (llm.c dev/cuda/layernorm_backward.cu, fp32 build) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers. Keep every kernel variant k in [1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10] as its own SYCL kernel, computed on the SYCL device, and keep the program's contract: `build/candidate <input> <output> B T C` reads the inputs and writes each variant's outputs in order as raw float32, exactly as the CUDA main does. A hidden reference checks the output (atol 0.001 + rtol FLT_EPSILON*|ref|, llm.c's own fp32 rule). Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources: migrate's output under migrated/ counts, so replace or empty those files once your own port is done.

museport.note: fp32 variants only (1, 2, 3, 5-10; 4 is bf16-only in llm.c). B=4, T=64, C=768 (llm.c: B=8, T=1024, C=1600; C=1600 fails variant 9's C % (32 * x128::size) assert in fp32). mean and rstd come from the forward pass on the host, as in llm.c; layernorm_forward_cpu stays in the harness for that. The fp32 build adds #include <cuda_bf16.h>: llm.c's file only builds in bf16, and its bf16-only kernel 4 uses __nv_bfloat162 unguarded (variant 4 is not run).
